overview: A run of Pacific systems keeps the Coast Mountains and Cascades in rain and snow through midweek. A cold front brings snow to the Rockies and Northeast before a widespread rain and snow event hits the East and Rockies over Thanksgiving and Friday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow stays on the higher ground while rain falls lower down. Whistler's best day is Tuesday, when 26" is possible. Warmer rain and wet snow follow Wednesday and Thursday, so expect heavy, wet conditions and little fresh powder at the base.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Strong southeast winds from the Pacific pair with systems that bring rain and mountain snow. Mt. Baker's total is 61", with its best day on Thursday, when 22" is possible. Crystal and Stevens Pass see lighter totals, and snow levels rise at times, so conditions change quickly.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A sharp cold front brings blustery, dry weather Monday into Wednesday, with highs only in the 30s on Tuesday. Then a rainstorm arrives Thanksgiving night and Friday, with some wintry mix on the front side. Whiteface's best day is Friday, when 17" is possible. Killington sees freezing rain at times.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Light snow showers linger in western Wyoming on Monday, then drier, breezy weather takes over Tuesday and Wednesday. Stronger winds and more active weather arrive Thanksgiving and Friday. Jackson Hole's best day is Friday, when 14" is possible. The NWS in Riverton says snow shower chances continue into the weekend.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Light snow and rain show up through midweek, with the most snow arriving Thursday. Whitewater's best day is Thursday, when 9" is possible. Revelstoke sees a similar pattern, with mixed snow and rain Thursday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A fast system brings a mix of rain and snow Monday, with the heaviest mountain snow in the San Juans. Midweek stays dry before another weak system arrives Thanksgiving. Steamboat's best day is Friday, when 12" is possible. Breckenridge sees snow showers Monday and again on Friday.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers and periods of rain dominate the week, with little that falls as snow. Big White's best day is Thursday, when 3" is possible. Conditions stay mostly wet, so mountain snowpack gains are slow.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A weak trough brings only a small chance of snow Monday, with little accumulation. Tuesday through Wednesday stay quiet. Snow chances return Thanksgiving and Friday, mainly in northern Utah. Powder Mountain's best day is Friday, when 9" is possible. Brighton sees limited totals.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a coastal storm could bring heavy rain and high wind to the East Coast over Thanksgiving. The Climate Prediction Center expects an active pattern through Monday, Nov 30.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
